excludedAssessments.summary: The internal audit establishes, relative to the supplied transcription, the exact 30-row private-message expansion, preservation under input-only product marginalization, the optimization inequalities, and well-definedness of V_0(g,k). However, the composite claim also asserts faithful reproduction of the external Gohari–Liu–Nair Theorem 9, and the record neither supplies authenticated source text nor performs a semantic comparison with that theorem. Therefore the full claim is not established.
scopeQualifications: The 30-row equivalence is valid only relative to the supplied transcribed system and executable local formulation: 26 min-expanded equation rows plus four scalar side-condition rows.

The product-marginalization proof preserves every audited single-output information term and both side conditions, provided the transcription is exhaustive and faithful; it cannot be extended unconditionally to the external theorem without source verification.
The inequalities V_Q(G,K) <= V(1/2;G,K) <= B(G,K) follow directly from feasible-set restriction and the definition of B; the restricted feasible set is nonempty and the relevant rates are bounded.

For the transcribed system, every Q0-supported information term depends on each binary-input receiver channel only through its fair-prior Jensen gap, with endpoint gaps zero; hence the channel dependence is through (c,g,k,c), making V_0(g,k) unambiguous on its stated domain.
evidenceIssues: No reviewed PDF bytes or independently authenticated primary-source text were supplied.
The attested verifier was run without --source-pdf, so the asserted source hash and byte count were not authenticated.
Even optional source-PDF verification would check only hash and size, not semantically compare the displayed equations, side conditions, or factorization against the source.
The executable audit does not encode or check the claimed factorization.
Because exact primary-source fidelity is an essential conjunct of the declared claim, the otherwise verified internal algebra does not make the composite claim valid.
